verdict.rationale: Cline is itself an AI coding agent embedded in the editor and CLI, so users can delegate tasks to it directly. It creates files, runs commands, browses the web and uses tools. Plan/Act modes, auto-approve/YOLO and subagents support increasingly autonomous delegation, and hands-on community reports corroborate setting it loose on a codebase and returning to accurate diffs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can delegate tasks to a built-in AI assistant inside the product

citations.quote: AI coding assistant in your editor. Create files, run commands, browse the web, and use tools with human-in-the-loop approval.
Autonomous execution can modify files and run commands without further prompts.
Toggle Plan mode to align on a strategy, then Act to execute. Approve every step, or flip auto-approve for autopilot.
Subagents let Cline spawn focused research agents that run in parallel.
I can plan with it for 10-15 minutes, set it loose on my codebase, go get lunch, and then its diff is almost always completely on the money.
